title: Beyond Relevance: On the Relationship Between Retrieval and RAG Information Coverage
abstract: This work studies whether upstream retrieval measurements predict the information coverage of downstream RAG answers. Across text and multimodal RAG benchmarks, coverage-oriented retrieval metrics correlate more strongly with generated-response coverage than ordinary relevance metrics when the task requires broad information coverage. The results also show that iterative RAG can partially decouple final generation quality from initial retrieval effectiveness.

admission.reason: The abstract studies correlation between retrieval metrics and downstream information coverage, but does not implement a structured evidence-gap controller, verification-aware stopping rule, provenance mechanism, or calibrated stopping policy. Its vocabulary is relevant to F4, but the required control capability is absent.

title: Score-Based Diffusion Priors for Adaptive Conformal Inference under Distribution Shift
abstract: DiffConf develops adaptive conformal inference for temporal and covariate distribution shifts using score-based diffusion priors plus online recalibration. It provides finite-sample marginal coverage guarantees while the data distribution evolves and analyzes additional coverage behavior under drift assumptions. This is transfer evidence for online risk calibration in a non-stationary RAG controller.

admission.reason: The paper is generic adaptive conformal inference under temporal or covariate shift rather than retrieval, RAG, QA abstention, or evidence stopping. Its transfer value is substantially duplicated by VERIFIED conformal-shift candidates in this set, especially 2208.08401, so the UNCHECKED candidate does not justify a reading slot.

title: RMIT-ADM+S at the MMU-RAG NeurIPS 2025 Competition
abstract: The paper presents R2RAG, which dynamically adapts retrieval strategy using query complexity and evidence sufficiency. For iterative cases, accumulated evidence is reviewed for coverage of query subparts and remaining knowledge gaps; further queries target those gaps, while stopping also respects a context-token threshold and a bounded iteration cap. The system was evaluated in the MMU-RAG competition's dynamic setting.

admission.reason: The abstract contains adaptive retrieval, query-subpart coverage checks, gap-targeted follow-up, a token threshold, and an iteration cap, but these capabilities substantially overlap the more explicit and experimentally stronger integrated controllers represented by MEGRAG, DynaKRAG, FAIR-RAG, and AdaGATE. Nothing in the abstract adds calibrated risk control, temporal/version provenance, permissions, or a distinctive cost model that would close the remaining high-priority gaps.

title: Towards Trustworthy Knowledge Graph Reasoning: An Uncertainty Aware Perspective
abstract: UAG introduces conformal uncertainty quantification into multi-step reasoning that combines knowledge graphs and language models. An error-rate control module allocates error rates across components of the multi-step process so the overall system can achieve a predefined coverage target. Although not an iterative document-RAG stopping controller, it is directly relevant to distributing a calibrated risk budget across structured evidence-acquisition and reasoning stages.

admission.reason: The abstract concerns conformal uncertainty allocation across knowledge-graph and language-model reasoning components, not document retrieval, RAG evidence acquisition, retrieval stopping, or provenance-aware investigation. The risk-budget idea is transferable in principle, but the capability is too indirect for this constrained round and the identifier is UNCHECKED.

title: Selective Classification Under Distribution Shifts
abstract: The paper develops generalized selective classification for deployment data containing in-distribution, covariate-shifted, and label-shifted or out-of-distribution samples. It studies confidence functions for deciding which cases should be rejected so that error on the retained predictions is controlled more reliably under shift. The framework is transfer evidence for abstention and risk-coverage evaluation of RAG controllers.

admission.reason: This is general selective classification under mixed distribution shifts rather than QA or retrieval. F5 already has a more task-aligned VERIFIED selective-QA candidate, and the broader classification formulation does not materially strengthen evidence-gap retrieval or stopping beyond that transfer evidence.

title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Distribution Shift
abstract: Adaptive conformal inference constructs online prediction sets when the data-generating distribution changes over time in an unknown way. It continuously adapts the conformal control parameter and provably achieves the desired long-run coverage frequency without requiring an exchangeable stream. This is foundational transfer work for calibrating a stopping or abstention controller on a non-stationary evidence stream.

admission.reason: Adaptive conformal inference under evolving distributions is relevant transfer theory, but this round already contains a more directly task-aligned selective-QA-under-shift paper and a later VERIFIED online conformal paper explicitly handling arbitrary distribution shifts. Reading this additional generic foundation is unlikely to change the project decision or close gap-3.

title: URAG: A Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
abstract: URAG benchmarks uncertainty quantification for retrieval-augmented language models across domains and multiple RAG methods, including conformal-prediction-based approaches. Its experiments vary retrieval depth, retrieval noise, and other contextual factors that affect confidence reliability. The benchmark is relevant for evaluating whether a stopping confidence signal remains calibrated as retrieval conditions change.

admission.reason: URAG evaluates uncertainty methods under changes in retrieval depth and retrieval noise, which is useful benchmarking context, but the abstract does not describe a retrieval controller, calibrated stopping rule, selective-answer policy under domain shift, or risk guarantee. It measures signals that a controller could use rather than providing the missing capability itself.

title: High Probability Risk Control Under Covariate Shift
abstract: This paper extends high-probability Learn-Then-Test risk control to covariate shift by importance-weighting calibration losses. It targets finite-sample control of user-specified risks when calibration and deployment distributions differ and validates the method on fraud detection and image classification. The method is a transferable candidate for calibrating RAG stopping policies when the query distribution shifts.
venue: Fourteenth Symposium on Conformal and Probabilistic Prediction with Applications

admission.reason: The method provides generic finite-sample risk control under covariate shift and is tested outside retrieval or QA. Its possible transfer to RAG stopping is indirect, it is UNCHECKED, and VERIFIED candidates in this set provide either RAG-specific conformal risk analysis or QA-specific selective prediction under shift.

title: Survey of Temporal Information Retrieval and Related Applications
abstract: This survey organizes the temporal information-retrieval literature and reviews methods that exploit temporal information in documents and queries. It distinguishes multiple temporal search needs, summarizes temporal query analysis and retrieval models, and discusses open problems in end-to-end temporal retrieval. The survey provides transfer context for separating ordinary recency ranking from richer temporal evidence requirements.

admission.reason: This is a survey organizing temporal information-retrieval terminology and prior methods rather than a candidate controller or empirical study that closes the current gaps. It may be useful as background vocabulary, but it does not itself validate structured temporal gaps, version-aware iterative retrieval, or temporally grounded stopping, and the identifier is UNCHECKED.
